episode_row: memory_growth false CRITICAL; one unexplained restart

commits.subject: fix(health): tune memory_growth thresholds based on real prod RSS
commits.body:
First end-of-day health-check cycle on 2026-04-28 fired a spurious
CRITICAL alert for the scheduler at 2.9 GB RSS. Original thresholds
(INFO 200MB / WARN 500MB / CRITICAL 1024MB) were calibrated against
the SLEEPING-state baseline (~90 MB) — but the scheduler's bts-run
path loads 1.5M PA × dozens of features into pandas + trains 12 LightGBM
blend models in process. That legitimately allocates 2-3 GB which
CPython doesn't return to the OS.

Post-prediction baseline is fundamentally different from sleeping
baseline. New thresholds:
  INFO 1024 MB:    notable growth, worth observing
  WARN 3072 MB:    significant — beyond expected post-prediction RSS
  CRITICAL 6144 MB: ~40% of bts-mlb 16 GB, likely real leak

Test added for the 2.9 GB regression case (INFO not CRITICAL).
After deploy, tonight's 21:21 ET CRITICAL would have been INFO instead.

The misfire ALSO triggered an unintended bts-scheduler restart
(NRestarts: 0 → 1) — root cause unclear from journal, possibly
systemd watchdog timeout under high RSS. Worth follow-up but
unblocked by the threshold tune.
